title: 2018 AMC 8 Problem 9
statement: Tyler is tiling the floor of his \(12\) foot by \(16\) foot living room. He plans to place one-foot by one-foot square tiles to form a border along the edges of the room and to fill in the rest of the floor with two-foot by two-foot square tiles. How many tiles will he use?

solutions.text:
Note that each square foot of the border would require one tile, meaning that the border will take \(16+12+16+12=56\) tiles. However, notice that this will cause overlapping tiles in each of the four corners, so to fix this, we subtract \(4.\) Therefore, the border will take \(56-4=52\) \(1\times 1\) square tiles to completely tile.

Since we have removed one foot from each side due to the border, the remaining rectangle is \(10\) feet by \(14\) feet. This must be tiled completely by \(2 \times 2 \) tiles, so it will take \[ \dfrac{10\cdot14}{2\cdot2} = 35 \] tiles in total to tile this area.

As it takes \(52\) \(1\times 1\) square tiles to tile the border, and \(35\) \(2\times 2\) square tiles to tile the remaining area, it will take \(52+35=87\) tiles in total to fill in Tyler’s entire living room floor.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Count the \(1\)-foot border tiles first, being careful not to double-count the corners.
After removing a \(1\)-foot border, the remaining rectangle is \(10\) feet by \(14\) feet.
